name: Ash glazing
summary: A glaze that comes from wood or plant ash. The ash melts with the clay and makes a green, yellow or brown glass.
how: Burn wood or straw and sieve the ash.
Wash the ash to take out the soluble salts.
Mix it with clay and feldspar, or use it alone.
Pour or dip the glaze and fire to 1250 °C or more.

origin.note: Ash falls on pots in a wood-fired kiln and melts into a thin green glaze.

adoptions.via: Hamada Shōji settles in Mashiko and mixes ash glazes from local plant ash and rock, and fires them in a wood-fired kiln.
Studio potters fire wood-ash and shino glazes on stoneware plates that they make with chefs.
